text: Apollinary Mikhaylovich Vasnetsov (Russian: Аполлина́рий Миха́йлович Васнецо́в; 6 August [O.S. 25 July] 1856 – 23 January 1933) was a Russian painter and graphic artist who specialised in scenes from the medieval history of Moscow. He did not receive a formal artistic education and studied under his older brother, Viktor, also a renowned painter. From 1883, he lived and worked alongside Viktor at Abramtsevo, where he was influenced by Vasily Polenov. Between 1898 and 1899, Vasnetsov travelled across Europe. In addition to epic landscapes of Russian nature, he developed a unique genre of historical landscape reconstruction based on historical and archaeological data, presenting a visual depiction of medieval Moscow. He joined the Association of Travelling Art Exhibitions (Peredvizhniki) in 1899 and became an academician in 1900. He was one of the founders and supervisors of the Union of Russian Artists. Vasnetsov had three elder and two younger brothers; his only sister died at four months old. His father played a significant role in the upbringing and education of his sons, teaching them to love nature and observe the lives of birds and animals. The death of his father in 1870 was a severe emotional blow to Vasnetsov. In 1890, he made a journey across the North of the Russian Empire, recording beautiful views of Siberia and the Urals, which inspired paintings such as those depicting these regions. In 1895, Vasnetsov visited the Caucasus, where he was deeply impressed by the rugged mountains; he climbed the glaciers of Mt. Elbrus, visited Tiflis, and lived in the Darial Gorge, creating numerous sketches during this time. In 1890, he also travelled to Europe, visiting France and Italy, where he studied the works of famous masters. At the beginning of 1920, the Committee of Archaeology (the predecessor of the Community for the Saving of Art Monuments) invited Vasnetsov and other painters, including Vikentii Trofimov, to draw the old places of Voronezh. A minor planet, 3586 Vasnetsov, discovered by Soviet astronomer Lyudmila Zhuravlyova in 1978, is named after both Viktor Vasnetsov and Apollinary Vasnetsov.
